title: Site configuration
description: The hand-written site.yaml that describes one site: identity, boundary, default view, and how the pipeline selects walkways.

id.description: Directory name under sites/ and the site segment of share URLs.

short_name.description: A brief name shown under the icon when the site is installed to a phone's home screen, where long names are cut off. Around 12 characters fit. Defaults to the name.

operator.description: Who runs this site. Named on the privacy page, with any contact given, so a visitor knows whom to ask about it.

name.description: The organization or person, as it should read after 'is run by'.

email.description: An address for questions about the site.

url.description: A web page for questions about the site; https only.

boundary.description: The area OpenStreetMap data is fetched for. Exactly one of the three forms.

view.description: Where the map opens before a position is known.

units.description: How distances are shown: meters and kilometers, or feet and miles.

categories.description: The kinds of place this site has, in the order the map legend lists them, each with the name people read. A kind's position in the list also decides its color on the map. Kinds the site's places use but this list leaves out are added after it, named from their value.

id.description: The category value places carry, such as call_box.

label.description: The name shown in the legend, such as Call boxes.

nearest.description: Place categories that get a one-tap "nearest" button. Each entry names a category used by this site's places and the label its button shows. Nearest is measured by walking distance over the network, not straight-line.

category.description: A category value as used in places.yaml.

label.description: The word shown on the button and read to a screen reader, for example "Parking" or "Call box".

safety.description: Telephone numbers for someone who needs help, listed in the app's Safety panel in this order: emergency services, the site's own security office, helplines. Each is offered as a number the phone can call. Left out, the app shows no Safety panel.

label.description: Who answers, for example "Emergency" or "Campus security".

number.description: The number as people write it, for example "911" or "(352) 555-0100". Digits, with spaces, brackets, hyphens and dots between them as wished, and a leading plus for a country code. Quote it in YAML so it stays text.

note.description: A few words on when to use the number or when it is answered.

walkways.description: Which OpenStreetMap highway values count as walkways for this site.

unpaved.description: Surface values that make a way unusable here, replacing the default list.

max_connector_m.description: A place whose entrance is further than this from a walkway is reported.

snap_m.description: How far a hand-drawn walkway's end may be from a mapped walkway and still be joined to it.

join_crossings.description: Whether walkways that cross at ground level without sharing a point are joined where they cross. OpenStreetMap treats such a crossing as unconnected, which is right for a bridge and usually an omission elsewhere; ways tagged as a bridge, a tunnel, or on another layer are never joined. Off by default.

parking_aisles.description: Whether the aisles of parking lots count as walkways. On by default: people walk through lots, and the router can still prefer sidewalks.

roads.description: Highway values of roads a pedestrian may walk along when nothing better exists; they join sidewalks and parking aisles into one network. Replaces the default list.

routing.description: How the router weighs the network. Omitted values take the defaults given here.

weights.description: Cost multiplier per edge kind: a route's cost is meters times the kind's weight, so a weight of 3 makes a road worth walking only when every alternative is more than three times longer. Weights are at least 1.

walking_speed.description: Meters per second, used for the time estimate shown with a route.

tiles.description: Where the site's base map tiles are extracted from. The pipeline's tiles command reads only the tiles covering the site's data, plus a margin and, at the zoom levels the map can show, a ring of neighboring tiles, from a planet-wide PMTiles archive and writes basemap.pmtiles into the site directory.

source.description: URL of a PMTiles archive that answers HTTP range requests, for example a dated Protomaps basemap build.

margin_m.description: How far beyond the site's walkways and places the extract reaches, in meters.

max_zoom.description: Highest zoom level to extract; the source's own maximum when omitted. The map overzooms beyond it.

imagery.description: An aerial photograph of the site, offered as a layer of the map. The pipeline's imagery command fetches one picture covering the site from the service named here and stores it with the site's data, so the app serves it itself and no phone contacts the service.

source.description: URL of an ArcGIS ImageServer, without a trailing operation, for example a government orthoimagery service. Use only imagery you may redistribute.

attribution.description: The credit shown beside the layer's switch, naming whose imagery it is and from when.

name.description: The layer's name in the layers panel. 'Aerial photo' by default.

resolution_m.description: Meters on the ground per pixel. A site too large for this in one picture of 4000 pixels a side is fetched more coarsely. 0.6 by default.

margin_m.description: How far beyond the site's walkways and places the photograph reaches, in meters. 100 by default.

overlays.description: Images of the site's own maps, georeferenced by control points: a pixel in the image paired with the OpenStreetMap element or the position it depicts.

image.description: PNG file, relative to the site directory.

publish.description: Whether the overlay is served to people using the map. Set false to hold back an image the site may not show yet: it stays in the maintainer's checking page and is left out of the built image. True by default.

pixel.description: Column then row, from the top-left corner of the image.

position.description: Longitude then latitude, as GeoJSON orders them.

bbox.description: South, west, north, east in degrees, the order Overpass uses.
